title: Rangitoto Summit Track: Rangitoto Island, Auckland region
overview: Experience Auckland’s iconic island volcano as you’ve never seen it before. Discover fields of black lava, pōhutukawa forest alive with rare native birds, and views worth every step.
No dogs. Other pets on conservation land rules.

Easy to intermediate walking track
2 hr / 7 km (return)

From here, it's 2 min to Rangitoto Summit Lookout – a great picnic spot. You'll get panoramic views of Auckland/Tāmaki Makaurau and the Hauraki Gulf/Tīkapa Moana. There's seating and a historic fire command post – a remnant of the island's military history.
20 min / 850 m (loop)
15 min / 500 m (one way)
Lava Caves Track is signposted from Summit Track on your right (going up). The turnoff is 45 min from Rangitoto Wharf, and 15 min from the summit.
1 hr / 1.4 km (one way)
Wilson's Park Track is signposted from Summit Track on your left (going up). The turnoff is 40 min from Rangitoto Wharf.
25 min from Queens Wharf, in downtown Auckland
20 min from Devonport, on Auckland's north shore.
Ferry timetable and fares
Experienced kayakers can reach Rangitoto Wharf by kayak. It takes about 2 hr from Devonport or Takapuna Beach.
Bookings are not required for Rangitoto Summit Walk.
Camping is not permitted. Historic baches are available to book for overnight stays through Rangitoto Island Historic Conservation Trust .
Ōkura Bush Walkway is closed from the south end, between Haigh Road entrance and Karepiro Bay. This track is part of Te Araroa Trail.
